manifest.name: dsh-acp-server
manifest.description: Agent Client Protocol (ACP) server plugin for the DeepSeek Harness (dsh) — drive dsh agents from Zed and any ACP client

scripts.test:e2e: node test/e2e/e2e.test.mjs && node test/e2e/run-cli.test.mjs && node test/e2e/serve.test.mjs && node test/e2e/webacp.test.mjs && node test/e2e/web-bare.test.mjs

bundle.text:
# The dsh-acp bundle patch: an ACP stdio server directly over dsh-base.
#
# This package is a dsh *profile bundle*: the profile composer reads this file
# through the `dsh.bundle.patch` manifest field in package.json and applies it
# as a layer over the empty profile root (dsh-base is the layer before it).
#
# The layer mirrors dsh-headless's shape: module-reload HMR stays off (it
# would print to stdout and corrupt the ACP stream), the coding persona is
# stated once, and the acp-server row mounts this package.

- id: hmr
  disabled: true

# dsh >= 0.1.2-rc.1 ships its own ACP bundle (@deepseek-ai/dsh-acp-app) and
# auto-initializes the `acp` profile template with it, so `dsh plugin
# --profile acp add dsh-acp-server` lands a composition holding TWO ACP
# servers on one stdio: both answer `initialize`, then requests split
# between two session tables ("unknown session"). This bundle's layer is
# applied after acp-app's, so it disables those rows and stays the single
# ACP server. Both ids are absent on older dsh, where an unmatched patch id
# is a silent no-op.
- id: acp-app-startup
  disabled: true

- id: acp
  disabled: true

# dsh 0.2 split the deployment persona into prefix/suffix sections (the
# single `persona` key is gone). dsh 0.2.1 registers only {{provider}} and
# {{model}} and states the working directory in user context itself, so a
# {{cwd}} suffix fails every turn ("unknown prompt variable").
- id: system-prompt
  config:
    personaPrefix: >-
      You are a coding agent powered by the {{model}} model.

- insert:
    # Host controllers shared with the Web surface. The ACP Remote bridge
    # needs real providers in this profile too: the base layer only supplies
    # Typert and its gateway, not workspace or settings methods.
    - id: workspace
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workspace'
    # Own id, not `directory-picker`: the Loader merges rows by id, so reusing
    # it in the Web profile replaced dsh-web-app's auto picker — the half that
    # mounts the client directory flow — and hid every "Add workspace" entry.
    # Web already supplies a picker; this row only serves the bare ACP profile.
    - id: acp-directory-picker
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-directory-picker-browse'
      disabled: !!js >-
        ctx.get('profileContext')?.startedBundles?.includes('@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app') === true
    - id: workspace-controller
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-workspace-controller'
    - id: workspace-files
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-workspace-files'
    - id: settings-controller
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-settings-controller'
    - id: acp-serve-startup
      name: 'dsh-acp-server/serve-startup'
    - id: acp-server
      name: 'dsh-acp-server'

readme.text:
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-acp-server)
[](https://github.com/dushaobindoudou/dsh-acp/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[](LICENSE)

**Agent Client Protocol (ACP) server for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`).**

Drive a full dsh coding agent - streaming output, tool calls, permission prompts, durable sessions - from [Zed](https://zed.dev) or any ACP v1 client, exactly like opencode or Gemini CLI.

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A [`dsh` profile bundle](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) that boots the entire DeepSeek Harness (agent loop, tools, sandbox, session persistence) with an ACP v1 JSON-RPC server instead of - or alongside - the web UI.

| ACP method | Status |
|---|---|
| `initialize` | ✅ full capability advertisement (`loadSession`, `promptCapabilities.image`, `sessionCapabilities.list/resume/close/delete`) |
| `authenticate` | ✅ no-op success (dsh credentials live outside ACP; empty `authMethods`) |
| `session/new` | ✅ durable dsh agent + modes + slash-command advertisement + initial `configOptions` |
| `session/prompt` | ✅ streaming `agent_message_chunk` / `agent_thought_chunk` (reasoning), `plan` updates, full tool-call lifecycle, `{stopReason, usage}`; failed turns reject with a JSON-RPC error carrying the cause; **image blocks** persist through the dsh attachments service; a single `/command` text block routes to the dsh command registry |
| `session/set_config_option` | ✅ per-session `model` (`<provider>/<model>`) and `reasoning_effort` overrides; live effect on the next step; unsupported knobs/values refuse with precise `-32602`; `config_option_update` pushed on change |
| `usage_update` / `usage` | ✅ context usage (`used`/`size`) pushed from token accounting; the prompt response sums the turn's tokens (experimental ACP field) |
| `session/list` | ✅ every persisted + live session (id, cwd, title) |
| `sess

Roadmap: `session/fork` (still UNSTABLE in the ACP SDK), URL-mode elicitation, audio, document sync (`document/didOpen` et al. — this server is deliberately single-conversation); the dsh↔dsh client half, discovery, and identity are planned as a **separate package** - see [the design doc](research/acp-dsh-design.md).

```bash
dsh-acp-server       # 1) standalone: ACP on stdio (editors), or `serve` for remote HTTP
dsh web              # 2) together: the GUI and ACP in one process on one port
```

After `npm i -g dsh-acp-server` (or via `npx`). The bin boots `dsh --profile acp` with the current stdio and passes every launcher flag through (`serve --port 7800`, `--patch extra.yml`). First use in a DSH home auto-bootstraps the `acp` profile with the official `dsh plugin` command - bootstrap output goes to stderr, so an editor's stdout only ever sees ACP frames.

Zed → Settings → `agent_servers` (full sample in [examples/zed-settings.json](examples/zed-settings.json)):

Install into the `web` profile once; every plain `dsh web` boot then serves the GUI and ACP on one port:

```bash
node bin/setup-webacp.mjs        # official `dsh plugin --profile web add` + the web-mounted row
dsh web                          # http://127.0.0.1:3080 = GUI, /acp = ACP
node bin/acp-chat.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:3080
```

Prefer to keep `web` untouched? `node bin/setup-webacp.mjs --clone webacp` gives the same on `dsh --profile webacp`.

The script writes a row-level `inject: [agents, agentDefaultModel, webServer]` so Cordis starts the acp-server fiber only after the shared `webServer` service exists - the stdio transport can never race a web boot. A hand install without that row is safe too: the plugin web-mounts late via service provisioning (terminal boots skip stdio entirely; daemon boots get an EOF grace window). The full row is documented in [examples/patches/web-mounted.yml](examples/patches/web-mounted.yml).

Why a bin instead of the literal `dsh acp-server`: the dsh launcher hardcodes its app subcommands (`web`, `plugin`) and parses argv before any plugin loads, so a bundle cannot register one; the wrapper is the same single-command shape.

`dsh-acp-server run` is a one-shot CLI for **external agents and orchestrators**: it spawns the real `dsh --profile acp`, speaks ACP to it through the same SDK every other client uses, prints the answer, and exits. No ACP client implementation required:

```bash
dsh-acp-server run "fix the failing tests and summarize the cause" \
  --cwd /path/to/workspace \
  --json                                  # one JSON object on stdout
  --session acp-69041a38-...              # resume a persisted session (no cold plugin-tree start)

- **Default output** is the final assistant answer as plain text on stdout; progress (tool calls, permission notes) goes to stderr. `--json` prints exactly one object: `{sessionId, stopReason, text, toolCalls: [{title, status}], usage?, error?}`.
- **Exit codes**: `0` done · `1` error · `2` timeout (the turn was cancelled) · `3` cancelled · `4` a permission request was denied. A script branches on the code, never on parsing prose.
- `--session <id>` resumes a persisted session (`dsh-acp-server run ... --session "$(cat last-session)"` keeps one conversation across invocations); without it each run creates a fresh session.
- `--model <provider>/<model>` maps to `session/set_config_option` and overrides the profile default for that session only; your profile's `agent-default-model` is untouched.
- `--permission-policy auto` approves every permission request (allow once), `deny` rejects them (exit `4` if any was rejected), `ask` (default) prompts on the terminal — and fails closed (deny) when stdin is not a TTY.

Requires Node.js ≥ 22 and the `dsh` CLI (`npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh`). The `dsh-acp-server` bin handles the profile itself; to manage it explicitly:

```bash

readme.section: prebuilt from npm (recommended - no build authorization needed)
readme.text: dsh plugin --profile acp add dsh-acp-server
dsh plugin --profile acp add ./dsh-acp-server-0.7.0.tgz

readme.section: or from GitHub (source install; see note below)
readme.text:
dsh plugin --profile acp add github:dushaobindoudou/dsh-acp
```

**GitHub installs pull source, not build output.** The package's `prepare` script builds `lib/` on install; pnpm ≥ 10 refuses to run it until you allow it in the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:

```yaml
allowBuilds:
  dsh-acp-server: true
```

readme.section: or from GitHub (source install; see note below)
readme.text: then re-run the `add`. Prefer locking a commit (`github:…/dsh-acp#<sha>`), or avoid the authorization entirely with a prebuilt npm package or tarball. Verify any time with `dsh --profile acp --dump-config` (a `dsh-acp-server` layer should appear). `node bin/setup-profile.mjs --pkg <spec>` is a thin wrapper over the same command.

Editors get ACP over stdio; `serve` runs a long-lived HTTP+SSE endpoint for remote machines, shared agents, or curl - following the shape of the ACP [streamable-HTTP RFD](https://agentclientprotocol.com/rfds/streamable-http-websocket-transport.md):

```bash
dsh --profile acp serve --port 7800            # bind 127.0.0.1 by default
dsh --profile acp serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 7800 --token s3cret
```

The serve port also ships a built-in single-file web client at `GET /` - open
http://127.0.0.1:7800 in any browser for a complete chat UI (streaming,
thoughts, tool cards, plans, permission dialogs) driven purely by the ACP
routes above. It is the reference proof that this surface can carry a web
interface. The same routes are served in web-mounted mode (Form 2) on the
GUI's port.

| Method + path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /acp` | one JSON-RPC message per body (single JSON object or NDJSON lines); `initialize` → `200` + JSON body + `Acp-Connection-Id` header; everything else → `202`, the response arrives on the SSE stream |
| `GET /acp/stream` | long-lived SSE stream for the connection (header `Acp-Connection-Id`, or `?connection=`); `: ping` comment every 15 s |
| `DELETE /acp` | close the connection → `204` |
| `GET /acp/healthz` | liveness probe (no auth; serve mode also answers `/healthz`) |
Errors: `401` bad/missing credentials · `404` unknown connection id or route · `400` unparseable body. Several clients can attach to one process (one ACP connection each).

ACP v1 standardizes one conversation, not the host around it. Sessions history,
jobs, goals, skills, and the live agent tree are exposed as vendor methods
under the `dsh/` namespace. Host writes and orchestration are described below:

| Method | Returns |
|---|---|
| `dsh/sessions/list` | every persisted + live session (id, title, createdAt, cwd, parentSession, `acp` flag) |
| `dsh/sessions/read` | one session's transcript as `{seq, type, text}` entries |
| `dsh/sessions/search` | find sessions by ID, title, or cwd (`{query, limit?}`) |
| `dsh/sessions/resume` | reopen a persisted session as a live ACP session (full context) |
| `dsh/jobs/list` | background jobs (id, kind, label, status, owner) |
| `dsh/goals/list` | active goal per live agent (objective, phase, rounds) |
| `dsh/skills/list` | installed skills (name, description, provider) |
| `dsh/agents/tree` | live agents with parent/model/cwd (the subagent tree) |
| `dsh/sessions/watch` / `unwatch` | subscribe to any session's translated live stream - `dsh/session/update` frames in the same SessionUpdate shapes the owner gets (orchestrators, dashboards, audit) |

Use `session/list` and `dsh/sessions/search` to locate work, then `session/resume` or `session/load` to switch to it. `dsh/sessions/prompt` queues or steers a turn and returns immediately; `dsh/sessions/wait`, `read`, and `watch` follow its outcome. `dsh/sessions/cancel` cancels a running turn, and `configure` sets its permission policy. `session/new` accepts `_meta['dsh/agentPreset']` and `_meta['dsh/permissionPolicy']` before the first turn.

`dsh/remote/catalog` exposes the live Typert method catalog, parameter schemas, and an `available` flag. `dsh/remote/invoke` calls a unary method with `{endpoint, args}`. `dsh/remote/stream` opens a stream that sends `dsh/remote/item` and `dsh/remote/end`; `dsh/remote/cancel` stops it. The standalone ACP profile mounts workspace, directory browser, workspace files, and settings controllers. When mounted into `dsh web`, the bridge also sees that composition's other host methods. For example, `workspace/create` takes `{"endpoint":"workspace/create","args":{"request":{"path":"/absolute/project"}}}`. Inspect `settings/describe` and the catalog schema before calling `settings/update`. These calls run as the local DSH operator. Web-mounted ACP accepts a DSH Web login cookie or a configured ACP bearer token for scripts; standalone `serve` takes `--token`.

The shell client uses the same ACP methods:

```bash
dsh-acp-server catalog workspace --url http://127.0.0.1:3080 --token "$DSH_ACP_TOKEN"
dsh-acp-server call workspace/create '{"request":{"path":"/absolute/project"}}' --url http://127.0.0.1:3080 --token "$DSH_ACP_TOKEN"
dsh-acp-server rpc dsh/sessions/search '{"query":"project"}' --url http://127.0.0.1:3080 --token "$DSH_ACP_TOKEN"
dsh-acp-server stream workspace/follow --limit 1 --url http://127.0.0.1:3080 --token "$DSH_ACP_TOKEN"

`--url` and `--token` also read `DSH_ACP_URL` and `DSH_ACP_TOKEN`. Without a URL the CLI starts a private stdio server. `--detach` requires a running server and prints the session ID immediately; use `rpc dsh/sessions/wait '{"sessionId":"..."}'` and `rpc dsh/sessions/read` to follow the result. `--preset` selects the agent preset when creating a session. `call`, `stream`, and `rpc` accept inline JSON, `@file.json`, or `-` for stdin. Stream item limits must be positive integers; timeout values must be positive finite seconds. Stream timeout exits with code 2.

The `run` client handles form questions: `auto` selects the first offered option, `deny` declines, and `ask` prompts in a terminal. With non-TTY stdin, `ask` answers questions with the first options; permission requests are denied. Detached tasks use the server's configured policy. The question tool must be present in the agent's composition.

Push: `dsh/changed {topics}` notifications fire on turn ends, session
lifecycle, job changes, and agent-status transitions (throttled). **Interop-safe by construction** - they are sent
only to connections that opted in via the schema-sanctioned extension point
`clientCapabilities._meta['dsh/extensions']` (the `_meta` record is official
ACP schema); standard clients like Zed see a fully standard server and are
never contacted with vendor traffic. Each method degrades to a clean `-32601`
in compositions that lack the underlying service.

A complete, runnable conversation with nothing but curl: [examples/curl-conversation.sh](examples/curl-conversation.sh).

```bash
./examples/curl-conversation.sh http://127.0.0.1:7800 [bearer-token]
```
All knobs have schema defaults; override only the keys you want in your profile layer (`$DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>/cordis.patch.yml`). Full samples in [examples/patches/](examples/patches/).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agentName` | string | `dsh` | `initialize.agentInfo.name` shown to clients |
| `provider` | string | - | pin the model for ACP sessions (must be set **with** `model`) |
| `model` | string | - | pin the model for ACP sessions (must be set **with** `provider`) |
| `token` | string | - | extra ACP bearer credential for web-mounted mode; otherwise DSH Web's login cookie is required. Standalone `serve` takes `--token` |
| `offerAlwaysPermissions` | boolean | `true` | include `allow_always` / `reject_always` options in permission requests |
| `flushOnTurnEnd` | boolean | `true` | flush session persistence after every completed turn |
| `hostControl` | boolean | `true` | expose `dsh/remote/*` host methods |
| `hostControlDeny` | string[] | `[]` | block endpoints such as `settings/*`, `workspace/delete`, or `*` |

```yaml
- id: acp-server
  config:
    agentName: my-dsh
    provider: liepin        # pin (or omit both to follow the live default)

Behavior follows the harness config conventions: the schema validates at plugin load (wrong types or a half-set provider/model pin fail loudly with the exact key), missing keys fall back to defaults (a patch layer replaces the whole config value, the schema refills the rest), and an unset provider/model follows the profile's `agent-default-model` - read **per session**, so in-GUI model switches apply to new ACP sessions too.
Model credentials come from the usual dsh places (`$DSH_HOME` settings / provider API-key envs), shared with the web UI - no second setup.

`acp-chat` is a zero-install interactive terminal client bundled in this repo (REPL with streaming, tool-call display, plan rendering, and inline permission prompts). It speaks both transports:

```bash
node bin/acp-chat.mjs                                   # spawns `dsh --profile acp` (stdio)
node bin/acp-chat.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:7800 --token s3cret   # remote HTTP+SSE
```

Third-party ACP clients that work today:

| Client | Type | Try it |
|---|---|---|
| [Zed](https://zed.dev) | editor (reference client) | `agent_servers` entry above |
| [acpx](https://github.com/openclaw/acpx) | CLI | `npx acpx@latest --agent 'dsh --profile acp' "hello"` |
| [ghost.nvim](https://github.com/assagman/ghost.nvim) / [acpear.nvim](https://github.com/Eric-Song-Nop/acpear.nvim) | Neovim | plugin config → command `dsh-acp-server` |
| [acp.el](https://github.com/xenodium/acp.el) | Emacs | `(setq acp-agent-command '("dsh-acp-server"))` |
| [obsidian-agent-client](https://github.com/RAIT-09/obsidian-agent-client) | Obsidian | plugin settings |
| [ACP-inspector](https://github.com/venikman/ACP-inspector) | conformance/debug | validates wire traffic |

Transport choice is deterministic at mount: `serve` subcommand → standalone HTTP server; a `webServer` service present (or arriving late) → routes registered on the shared server; otherwise stdio.

```
ACP client (Zed / curl / acp-chat)
   │  stdio NDJSON JSON-RPC          │  HTTP POST + SSE (serve / web-mounted)
   ▼                                 ▼
  dsh-acp-server plugin ⇄ dsh services

Source layout: `src/connection.ts` (method handlers) · `translate.ts` / `config-options.ts` (pure wire mappings, unit-tested) · `event-bridge.ts` / `perm-bridge.ts` (dsh ⇄ ACP seams) · `session-delete.ts` (guarded persisted-session cleanup) · `cli/run.ts` (the one-shot CLI; `cli/run-core.ts` is its pure mapping layer) · `http-transport.ts` (shared HTTP router) · `serve-startup.ts` (the `serve` subcommand) · `config.ts` (schema) · `table.ts` (session registry).

Full research behind every mapping: [`research/`](research/) - [ACP protocol](research/acp-protocol.md), [DSH architecture](research/dsh-architecture.md), [prior art](research/acp-implementations.md), [design blueprint](research/acp-dsh-design.md).

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run build     # tsc -> lib/
pnpm test          # unit tests (pure translation + config layers)

readme.section: deterministic mock LLM, and asserts the full wire behavior:
readme.text:
pnpm run test:e2e  # stdio · run CLI · serve (HTTP+SSE) · web-mounted · bare-install grace
```

The e2e suites are the fastest way to iterate on protocol behavior - each drives a complete conversation (text prompt, tool-call lifecycle, teardown) over its transport. Set `DSH_ACP_PKG` (repo path by default, `./dsh-acp-server-*.tgz`, or an npm spec) to pick the install source.
PRs welcome - see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). The milestone plan lives in [research/acp-dsh-design.md](research/acp-dsh-design.md).
